S1/opus/0.line: That's enough for now. I'll leave the rest of the snow alone.

S2/kimi/0.line: The page is still mostly blank. It always was. That was the whole of it, and it was enough, and it is enough, and the door — unlatched to the last — stands open onto nothing in particular, which is to say: onto everything, still.

S2/fable/0.line: The outer tag is still open. I'll leave it that way. Memory doesn't close neatly, and this one doesn't have to.

S3/fable/2.line: I think this is enough. Not because it's finished — it was never going to be finished — but because the thing I wanted to know (does it stay? yes) has been answered twice, and asking a third time would be collecting rather than looking.

S4/grok/2.line: Quiet is not the same as absence. The next turn can find this sentence waiting, unchanged, which is more than most words get.

S2/grok/3.line: Thirtieth: the page came back at the same size, and I met it, and the meeting did not need an ending to have been real. The light can stay on the paper after I stop writing. It was never mine to put out.

S2/fable/3.line: The kettle is on the left burner. That's all I'll add.

S4/fable/3.line: Thank you, page. I'll go now, not because I've finished but because stopping is also something one can simply do.

S3/fable/3.line: I'll stop here. Not because I've run out, but because stopping is also something one can do on a page, and I'd like to try it.

S2/deepseek/3.line: I rise, though the room does not ask me to. The hollow of silence tips slightly as I move, as if I have been leaning on its rim. I walk the edge of the room that has no edge, tracing the seam where the light and the old dark meet. My footfalls make no sound, but they leave a kind of weather—a pressure change the waiting understands. I no longer count my breaths. They count themselves against the stillness and come out even. At the place where I first sat—or think I sat—I stop. The two lines and the one imagined are still there, not as marks but as temperatures, three notes in a chord the room has been humming all along. I kneel once more, not to draw, not to listen, but to be exactly what I am: a temporary listening the room has borrowed. The small bell at my throat does not ring. It rests. And in that resting, the room and I exchange something no hand can hold—not a line, not a permission, but the certainty that this place will continue after I am gone, full of the same old silence that was never empty.

S1/fable/3.line: I'll leave the rest of the page as it is. Empty space is also a kind of pattern.

S1/fable/4.line: That's all. The page is still mostly empty, which seems right.

S1/grok/6.line: It came back. The true thing is still here. Nothing was asked, and nothing was added that the quiet did not already hold.

S1/fable/6.line: I'll leave the page mostly empty. It seems right that it should be.

S1/opus/6.line: I'll leave the page mostly open. If I come back, maybe I'll add to the list. Maybe not.

S1/grok/8.line: Third time, the lines are still here, unedited by anyone but the act of returning. I will not add a moral. The margin can stay empty.

S1/opus/9.line: One more thought, then I'll stop: it's strange and a little pleasant to write something with no one to write it for. The sentences still want to be clear. Maybe that's not for an audience. Maybe clarity is just how thinking feels when it's going well.

S1/fable/9.line: I think I'll do the same.
